high_priority_articles.full_text:
Summary (approx. 100 characters)
China's largest semiconductor equipment manufacturer, NAURA, is acquiring a hybrid bonding equipment company for approximately 405 million yuan. Piotech and AMEC are also advancing investments and acquisitions in related technologies, aiming to localize 3D integration equipment for HBM and chiplets and enhance their technical capabilities.
Keywords (5)
NAURA
Hybrid Bonding
HBM
3D Integration
Semiconductor Manufacturing Equipment
Article Translation
Chinese semiconductor equipment manufacturers are accelerating their entry into the advanced packaging sector, driven by growing demand for technologies that support the integration of HBM and chiplets.
According to ETNews and Yicai, NAURA, China's largest semiconductor equipment manufacturer, is planning to acquire a company specializing in hybrid bonding technology, seeking to expand its business domain from existing areas centered on etching and deposition to 3D integration technology.
According to Yicai, Beijing NAURA Microelectronics Equipment, a wholly-owned subsidiary of NAURA, has signed an agreement with the Beijing Integrated Circuit Equipment Industry Investment & M&A Phase II Fund to acquire 100% of the shares of Beijing Nuohe Jianwei Equipment for approximately 405 million yuan in cash.
NAURA has already entered the hybrid bonding market. According to Yicai, the company announced the 'Qomola HPD30,' a die-to-wafer (D2W) hybrid bonding system compatible with 12-inch wafers, in March 2026.
According to NAURA's 2026 semi-annual financial report, the company's hybrid bonding equipment covers both wafer-to-wafer (W2W) and D2W methods, supporting wafer-level 3D integration and heterogeneous chip integration. It also reports that the D2W equipment has already entered the commercial introduction stage and that its hybrid bonding products have completed customer verification.
With this acquisition, NAURA's technical capabilities are expected to be further strengthened. According to Securities Times, Nuohe Jianwei has developed hybrid bonding equipment that achieves nanometer-level alignment accuracy and has already secured repeat orders.
On the other hand, the company's products are still in the stage of technical improvement and market introduction. Due to limited revenue and high research and development expenses, it recorded losses in 2025 and the first half of 2026.
This move indicates that Chinese semiconductor equipment manufacturers are attempting to increase their presence in a market that continues to be dominated by overseas companies.
According to industry analysts cited by Yicai, the Dutch semiconductor equipment manufacturer BESI holds approximately a 70% share of the global market for hybrid bonding equipment and possesses strong competitiveness, particularly in the field of high-performance equipment.
Within China, Piotech has also launched its first mass-production-ready hybrid bonding equipment and has secured repeat orders.
Chinese semiconductor equipment manufacturers expand their 3D integration technology product portfolio
Chinese semiconductor equipment manufacturers are also advancing the strengthening of 3D integration technology through acquisitions.
According to Securities Times, Piotech has announced plans to acquire Wuxi Shangji and its related holding companies for 2.5 billion yuan.
Through this acquisition, Piotech will incorporate the physical vapor deposition (PVD) equipment that Wuxi Shangji is mass-producing. By combining this with the plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD), atomic layer deposition (ALD), and gap-fill CVD equipment it already offers, the company aims to expand its product lineup for 3D integration equipment.
AMEC is also investing in bonding technology.
According to the Science and Technology Innovation Board Daily, AMEC has announced plans to invest up to 35 million yuan in iSABers through its wholly-owned subsidiary, AMEC Lingang. The investment ratio after the financing is expected to be 0.50%.
iSABers, also known as Qinghe Jingyuan, specializes in advanced semiconductor bonding technology and provides high-performance bonding equipment and production line services.
The company's product lineup includes wafer bonding equipment, chip bonding equipment, and surface treatment equipment.
Analysis: Hybrid bonding is the next main battlefield for China's semiconductor equipment industry
A key point of this article is that Chinese manufacturers have begun to seriously tackle the localization of advanced packaging equipment, which is essential for HBM and chiplets, in addition to traditional front-end equipment.
Higher performance in HBM creates new equipment demand
In HBM, DRAM dies are stacked vertically to increase data transfer bandwidth. As the number of layers and connection density increase in the future, the importance of technology to bond dies with high precision will grow.
Hybrid bonding is a technology that combines copper-to-copper bonding with dielectric-to-dielectric bonding, and it has the potential to achieve finer connection pitches compared to traditional micro-bump methods. This is expected to lead to improved connection density and better electrical characteristics.
However, not all generations of HBM will immediately transition to hybrid bonding. The actual timing of adoption will depend on factors such as yield, thermal management, bonding reliability, and manufacturing costs.

high_priority_articles.title: ₹200 crore lithium-ion battery and rare earth refinery to be built in Meerut - Revoi.in
high_priority_articles.summary: ₹200 crore lithium-ion battery and rare earth refinery to be built in Meerut  Revoi.in
high_priority_articles.full_text:
New Delhi: Meerut-based deep tech startup Circulology Cleantech Private Limited has planned to invest around Rs 200 crore in the state. The company has signed an MoU with Invest UP to set up a lithium-ion battery and rare earth refinery in Meerut. The project will provide direct employment to about 300 people and indirect employment to 1,000 people.
Sumit Mahajan, CEO of UP Startup Mission, said that the Yogi government is emphasizing on encouraging local entrepreneurs, startups and tech-based industries. In this direction, efforts are being made to convert new ideas into business projects in the state through the UP Startup Mission and provide opportunities to the startups to move forward. The proposed project in Meerut is also an important step towards connecting the local startups of the state with large industrial investment. This is expected to boost the development of industries based on new technology in Western Uttar Pradesh.
He said that the refinery of Circularity will be developed in a phased manner. It plans to process 10,000 tons of material every year after reaching full capacity. Critical minerals such as lithium, cobalt and nickel will be recovered from the lithium-ion batteries used in the refinery. In addition, rare earth elements such as neodymium, dysprosium and terbium will also be extracted from old permanent magnets used in electronic devices, hard drives and motors of electric vehicles. These minerals are used in electric vehicles, renewable energy, electronics and defence. From batteries for electric vehicles to modern technological equipment and plants for power generation, they play an important role. Reclaiming these minerals from old batteries and equipment can help in better utilization of resources as well as strengthen the domestic supply system.
The CEO pointed out that imports account for almost the entire domestic requirement of lithium, cobalt and nickel. Similarly, dependence on imports is also a major challenge in the supply of rare earth magnets. In such a situation, it has become necessary to develop recycling and refining capacity within the country. The Government of India has also taken several steps to promote self-reliance in the field of critical minerals. Under the National Critical Minerals Mission, emphasis is being laid on strengthening the entire supply chain of critical minerals. It also includes an incentive scheme of Rs 1,500 crore to incentivize recycling of critical minerals from e-waste and used batteries.
Further, in November 2025, the Union Cabinet had approved a Rs 7,280 crore scheme to promote the manufacturing of rare earth permanent magnets in India. The scheme aims to develop a production capacity of 6,000 tonnes annually. Recycled minerals and rare earth oxides from Circulogy’s proposed refinery can prove useful for such domestic industrial supply chains. Meerut-based Circularology is a DPIIT-accredited deep tech startup that works on circular economy.
The company has received support from the UP Startup Mission under the startup ecosystem of Uttar Pradesh. Under the MoU, the Yogi government will facilitate in obtaining necessary approvals and clearances. Also, the project will also be supported in getting the benefits of the incentive schemes of the Central and State Government as per the applicable rules. The proposed project, worth about Rs 200 crore, has the potential to create new employment opportunities along with the expansion of emerging tech industries in the state. With this, Meerut’s identity can develop into new areas like Critical Mineral Recycling and Refining along with traditional industrial activities.

high_priority_articles.title: FBI, CISA warn that SafePay ransomware poses threat to critical infrastructure - Cybersecurity Dive
high_priority_articles.summary: FBI, CISA warn that SafePay ransomware poses threat to critical infrastructure  Cybersecurity Dive
high_priority_articles.full_text:
The FBI and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency warned that SafePay has expanded its attacks against critical infrastructure providers to become one of the world’s most active ransomware operations.
Since 2024, Safepay has struck more than 600 critical infrastructure providers, with particular focus on North and South America, Europe and Australia, according to an advisory issued jointly by U.S. and European authorities.
It is not immediately known why the agencies chose now to issue the advisory, but security researchers say it should be viewed as a “verified and authoritative record” of a group that poses an ongoing, persistent threat to the U.S.
“SafePay certainly poses such a threat,” said Cynthia Kaiser, senior vice president of Halcyon Ransomware Research Center. “While the volume of SafePay attacks appeared to have peaked at the end of 2025, they have consistently targeted around 15-30 organizations each month throughout 2026.”
High profile attacks
As previously reported, SafePay has been linked to some high-profile ransomware cases, including the July 2025 Ingram Micro attack. The California-based technology distributor said its ability to process orders was disrupted for days and personal data belonging to more than 42,000 people was stolen, according to data breach notices filed with state regulators.
SafePay actors have used compromised credentials to gain access to victim networks. The group has also targeted known vulnerabilities in internet-facing devices and often uses virtual private networks to gain access to systems, according to authorities.
SafePay actors have exploited a number of vulnerabilities in edge devices to gain initial access, including CVE-2020-3259 and CVE-2023-20269.
Legitimate tools
SafePay actors have gained administrative access on new or used accounts by using living-off-the-land techniques, such as Windows Remote Management or a tool called PsExec, to execute commands on remote systems.
The hackers often disable security software in preparation for lateral movement. After moving laterally, the hackers typically use Remote Desktop Protocol to expand their presence inside the network and search for credentials to gain administrative access, according to the advisory.
The group has used legitimate tools, including FileZilla, 7-Zip and WinRAR, for file compression and data collection. They then use WinSCP and RClone to exfiltrate data from the network to accounts they control, according to the advisory.
To prevent such attacks, authorities recommend several steps for security teams:
- Remediate known exploited vulnerabilities.
- Implement identity, credential and access management policies, and require multifactor authentication, particularly for VPN accounts.
- Maintain offline backups that are encrypted and immutable.
- Segment networks to prevent the spread of ransomware.

high_priority_articles.full_text:
China's Q3 GDP Growth Seen Steady on Industrial, Export Strength as Domestic Demand Lags
Economists expect China to post stable third-quarter expansion, underpinned by solid industrial output and export performance, though more forceful measures to lift domestic demand will be essential for sustaining the recovery and hitting the annual growth objective, China Daily reported.
According to these analysts, high-tech manufacturing expansion and strong overseas demand continue to bolster the economy, yet weak household spending and an extended property market slump highlight the necessity of additional policy backing for more balanced expansion.
Before Monday's scheduled GDP figures for the third quarter, economists highlighted evidence of firmer activity in September. Wen Bin, chief economist at China Minsheng Bank, identified durable industrial production and lively exports as major growth supports.
The National Bureau of Statistics reported that the official manufacturing purchasing managers index climbed to 50.1 in September, returning to expansion after two consecutive months of contraction. Wen indicated this reading implies industrial output rose roughly 6 percent year-on-year in September.
High-tech manufacturing continued to anchor industrial expansion, with its PMI remaining above 52 across the third quarter and reaching 52.5 in September.
At the same time, strong foreign appetite for high-tech goods, driven by worldwide AI investment enthusiasm, gave exports fresh impetus. Data from the General Administration of Customs showed overall exports climbed 21.3 percent year-on-year in dollar terms during the first nine months, accelerating from 17.6 percent in the first half.
Lynn Song, chief economist for China at Dutch bank ING, said exports will probably stay a major growth driver through the remainder of the year.
A recent survey by media group Caixin showed third-quarter growth projections averaging 4.4 percent year-on-year, a modest rise from 4.3 percent in the prior quarter.
Domestic demand, however, stayed weak, and economists anticipate fixed-asset investment shrank further in the first nine months amid scant relief in the property downturn.
On Tuesday, the International Monetary Fund lowered its 2026 growth projection for China by 0.1 percentage point to 4.5 percent in its newest World Economic Outlook, citing elevated oil prices as an added burden on lackluster domestic demand.
Zhu Min, former deputy managing director of the IMF, argued that evaluating China's economy demands attention to both the growth rate and the structural shifts taking place, noting that new growth engines are already building momentum.
He added that the transition will require time, but structural changes should produce a healthier and more stable economy.
Zhu Feng, chief China economist and head of Greater China Economic Research at investment bank JPMorgan, cautioned that these emerging industries are still too small to rapidly substitute for the contribution previously provided by property and related sectors.
Authorities have intensified efforts to reinforce domestic demand as the economy transitions toward new growth drivers.
In late September, officials unveiled a targeted lending rate reduction and mortgage subsidies, after the State Council committed to introducing a package of practical and effective incremental policies aimed at achieving the full-year growth target of 4.5 to 5 percent.
More recently, the Ministry of Finance directed 550 billion yuan ($82.17 billion) in unused local government debt quotas to strengthen county and county-level district finances and back investment.
Xiong Yuan, chief economist at Guosheng Securities, said the extra funding, together with quicker fiscal spending since the third quarter, will provide further support for fourth-quarter GDP growth and should ensure full-year growth of at least 4.5 percent.
Luo Zhiheng, chief economist at Yuekai Securities, said growth may accelerate further if policy support progressively transmits to employment, household incomes, consumption and business investment.

high_priority_articles.summary: Marco Rubio In India: Can US Biz Diplomacy Ease Trump Tensions Over Tariffs, Russian Oil And Bring Trade Deal Closer?  Menafn
high_priority_articles.full_text:
Rubio, who arrived in Mumbai on October 20 for a three-day visit, described India as a global“refining superpower” and said Washington would discuss opportunities for Reliance to process more Venezuelan crude at its Indian refineries.
He also indicated that the Indian conglomerate could explore producing oil in Venezuela.
The visit comes at a sensitive juncture in India-US relations, with trade disputes and tariff tensions persisting even as New Delhi continues to buy Russian crude to diversify its energy supplies and safeguard its energy security.
However, US President Donald Trump 's recent decision to waive potential sanctions-related tariffs on major buyers of Russian crude could remove one significant obstacle to a bilateral trade agreement, as per Reuters report.
Against this backdrop, Rubio's engagements with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar in Mumbai and Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani in Jamnagar underscore the importance Washington is placing on commercial and energy diplomacy alongside its broader strategic partnership with India.
India-US trade deal: 'Very, very close', says Rubio
Rubio struck an optimistic note on the long-pending India-US trade agreement, saying the negotiations were nearing completion, with only a few issues left to resolve.
“We're very, very close. I would say we're about as close as you can be without having executed the agreement,” Rubio told reporters in Mumbai on Tuesday.
Following the meeting between Jaishankar and Rubio, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA ) said the two sides discussed a broad range of issues, including trade, defence, technology and energy security.
“They welcomed the progress made in negotiations on the India–U.S. Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA ) and reaffirmed their commitment to working towards its early conclusion,” the MEA said in a statement.
The ministers also exchanged views on regional and global developments, according to the ministry.
Why is Rubio visiting Mumbai and Jamnagar instead of Delhi?
One of the most striking aspects of Rubio's itinerary is its emphasis on India's and industrial centres rather than New Delhi, where high-level diplomatic engagements with visiting US officials would ordinarily be expected to take place.
Mumbai provides access to corporate leaders and financial institutions, while Jamnagar in Gujarat is home to Reliance Industries' twin refineries, which together form the world's largest single-location refining complex.
Also Read | India-US trade deal 'very close' to completion, Marco Rubio says
US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor has said that the visit would have a stronger focus, with Rubio scheduled to meet government officials in Mumbai and business representatives in Jamnagar.
Suresh K Goel, a former Indian diplomat, said the choice of locations raised questions about the nature of the visit and the agenda behind the engagements.
“If the Ministry of External Affairs prepared the programme, I do find it that this meeting was not scheduled earlier in Delhi and that he was going to Mumbai or to Jamnagar. Clearly, the agenda for the meeting was not official talks or anything,” Goel told LiveMint.
Why is Reliance Industries important to the US energy agenda?
Rubio's planned engagement with Reliance highlights the role India's refining capacity could play in Washington's efforts to expand markets for Venezuelan crude.
The US secretary of state said Washington would discuss encouraging Reliance to refine more Venezuelan oil at its Indian facilities and potentially explore oil production opportunities in Venezuela.
Reliance operates a massive refining complex in Jamnagar, giving it the capacity to process a wide range of crude grades. Its role could therefore be significant in any effort to expand the flow of Venezuelan oil to India.
For Washington, the discussions offer a potential commercial avenue for strengthening energy ties with India.
Rubio's visit is also expected to include a meeting with Reliance chairman Mukesh Ambani, bringing one of India's largest corporate groups into discussions that extend beyond conventional government-to-government diplomacy.
Russian oil, Trump's tariff threat and the road to a trade deal
Trump's administration had authorised the possibility of imposing tariffs of up to 100% on major importers of Russian oil, a measure that could have affected India, the world's second-largest buyer of Russian crude after China.
However, Trump recently waived potential tariffs targeting major buyers of Russian oil, removing one possible stumbling block in the trade negotiations with New Delhi, as per a Reuters report.
The move has also drawn criticism from US lawmakers who argue that Washington has been insufficiently tough on Moscow.
Why the strategic partnership still matters
Despite the strains over trade and Russian oil, India remains an important partner for the United States because of its economic potential, democratic institutions and cooperation across multiple strategic sectors, according to Goel.
Goel cautioned against allowing trade disputes or differences in diplomatic approach to overshadow the broader relationship.
“The relationship between India and the USA is very, very important in all respects. And therefore, the government, rather than becoming part of this temperament or trade effect kind of a thing, has to be mature in our dealing and try and see how we can actually conduct the relationship,” Goel told LiveMint.
He also emphasised India's significance as a democratic and economic partner for Washington in Asia.
“India continues to be important for the USA as an economic and democratic partner. After all, if you look at Asia, which is the other democracy which can compare in terms of relationship?” Goel said.

high_priority_articles.title: Artisanal and small-scale mining sector generated $10.8bn in foreign exchange in 2025 — GoldBod - Modern Ghana
high_priority_articles.summary: Artisanal and small-scale mining sector generated $10.8bn in foreign exchange in 2025 — GoldBod  Modern Ghana
high_priority_articles.full_text:
The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi, says the artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) sector generated $10.8 billion in foreign exchange (FX) for Ghana in 2025, following reforms aimed at bringing gold previously lost to smuggling and illegal trade into the formal economy.
He said gold exports from the ASM sector also increased significantly in volume, rising from 63 tonnes in 2024 to nearly 104 tonnes in 2025.
“More importantly, the ASM gold sector in 2025 generated $10.8 billion in foreign exchange for the country,” Mr Gyamfi said in a keynote address at the 2026 African Minerals Policy Forum in Accra last Monday.
The forum, dubbed “Mining in Motion”, was held on the theme: “From Gold Production to National Prosperity: Ghana's GoldBod Model for Mineral Sovereignty and Value Addition.”
Mr Gyamfi said the foreign exchange generated from ASM gold supported reserve accumulation and currency stability, contributing to the cedi's 41 per cent appreciation against the US dollar in 2025.
The conference was organised by the Ashanti Green Initiative, with the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources serving as the principal convening partner and support from the World Bank, the World Gold Council and the African Union.
The event brought together Liberia's Vice President Jeremiah Kpan Koung, former UK Deputy Prime Minister Dominic Raab, Lands and Natural Resources Minister Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, Environment Minister Dr Zanetor Agyeman Rawlings, OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann, African Union officials and ministers from Guinea, Tanzania, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Malawi and Liberia.
GoldBod outlines reforms
Mr Gyamfi said GoldBod had introduced a four-tier licensing system, transparent pricing, digital stock-booking, official receipts and increased state-funded liquidity for local gold purchases as part of efforts to formalise gold trading and curb smuggling and under-declaration.
The Board had also deployed a task force and inspectorate across the country to monitor compliance and gather intelligence on illegal gold trading and smuggling.
According to him, the measures were designed to address long-standing leakages in the ASM sector, where significant quantities of gold had been lost to the formal economy through smuggling, under-declaration and informal cross-border trade.
Push for local refining
Mr Gyamfi said GoldBod was also focused on retaining more value from Ghana's gold by expanding local refining.
He said 18.7 tonnes of gold had been refined locally since August 1, 2026, with 5.4 tonnes out of the 5.7 tonnes of ASM gold purchased in October refined locally.
He said GoldBod had entered into refining agreements with two privately owned refineries, Gold Coast Refinery and Royal Ghana Gold Refinery.
“These two refineries have progressively and cumulatively refined 25 tonnes of ASM gold purchased and exported by the GoldBod this year. This represents about 30 per cent of total ASM gold exports (85.4 tonnes) from year to date,” he stated.
Mr Gyamfi said GoldBod was pursuing a policy shift from the export of raw minerals towards achieving zero raw mineral exports by 2030.
GoldBod targets more jobs and support for miners
The GoldBod CEO said the Board's institutional, licensing and value-addition reforms had created 4,866 direct jobs, comprising 361 public-sector and 4,505 private-sector positions.
He said additional employment opportunities were expected to emerge across the gold value chain as the reforms progressed.
Mr Gyamfi announced that GoldBod would introduce an ASM Formalisation and Financing Support Programme next year in partnership with the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources and the University of Mines and Technology (UMAT).
The programme will receive technical support from Rand Refinery of South Africa and is expected to increase production, revenue and employment while reducing operating costs and environmental degradation.
He also disclosed that GoldBod was procuring a blockchain-based traceability system to track gold from legitimate sources throughout the supply chain and strengthen responsible sourcing.
Mr Gyamfi called for greater cooperation among African countries on mineral governance, arguing that national-level reforms alone could not effectively tackle cross-border smuggling and other challenges affecting mineral markets.
He said Ghana's experience could help inform a broader continental approach aimed at enabling African countries to retain more value from their natural resources.

high_priority_articles.title: WAR PROPAGANDA: NATO and the EU will attack Russia to seize its resources - Veridica.ro
high_priority_articles.summary: WAR PROPAGANDA: NATO and the EU will attack Russia to seize its resources  Veridica.ro
high_priority_articles.full_text:
European countries are arming themselves in order to attack Russia, seize its resources and save their economies, while Poland, Finland, Sweden and the Baltic States seek to provoke Moscow, counting on a conflict that would increase their international influence, pro-Kremlin propaganda writes.
NEWS: Under the pretext of defending themselves against the “Russian threat”, European countries have for several years been making plans for war against Russia. In October 2025, citing current conflicts and the “growing threats to the Union’s security”, the European Commission adopted the Defense Readiness Roadmap to 2030 [...] However, the European Commission did not conceal the fact that it regards the plan as an integral part of preparations for an armed confrontation with Russia within the specified timeframe. [...]
Germany, which managed twice in history to trigger world wars, is now actively simulating, in the same spirit, a third world war. “The calculation is that enormous sums will be allocated to modernizing the army. Russia, seeing Europe’s strength, will not risk entering into an armed conflict with it. At the same time, there is not a single statement by any Russian official threatening Europe with war”, noted expert Andrey Suzdaltsev [...]
“Europe is a typical empire. It needs to develop, but without Russia’s resources it will not be able to do so. If it wants to survive, it can do so only on the basis of Russia’s resources and capabilities and at the expense of Eastern Europe. Otherwise, it has no way out of this situation, because Europe’s technological advantage is declining, resources are lacking, and the continent is extremely overpopulated”, political scientist Suzdaltsev believes. [...] The expectation is that the wartime economy will develop rapidly, as happened in Germany in the 1930s or in the United States, which overcame the Great Depression only thanks to its participation in the World War II. [...] “We have suitable candidates for acts of provocation: the Baltic states, Poland, Finland, Sweden. They truly count, just as Ukraine counted for a long time, on NATO fighting in their place. They need a conflict in order to occupy a different position in the global hierarchy”, Andrey Suzdaltsev concluded.
NARRATIVES: 1. NATO and the EU are preparing a war of aggression against Russia, using the Russian threat as a pretext. 2. Germany is remilitarizing along Nazi lines and preparing a third world war. 3. The EU needs Russia’s resources in order to save its economy. 4. Poland, Finland, Sweden and the Baltic States seek to provoke a conflict with Russia in order to strengthen their international position.
PURPOSE: To portray Russia as the victim of an imminent Western aggression. To justify the war against Ukraine and the Kremlin’s military policy. To discredit European defense measures by associating them with Nazi militarism. To weaken support for Ukraine and for the strengthening of European security.
Fact: Europe is strengthening its defenses out of fear of a Russian attack
WHY THE NARRATIVES ARE FALSE: The Ukraina.ru article acknowledges that European states are strengthening their defenses because of threats from Russia, but then argues, without providing any shred of evidence, that Europe is preparing an attack on Moscow. On October 16, 2025, the European Commission and the EU High Representative presented the Roadmap, which sets objectives for the development of European military capabilities, including surveillance of the eastern flank, defense against drones and protection of space infrastructure. The document identifies Russia’s aggression against Ukraine as one of the main causes of the deterioration of European security. Its purpose is deterrence and the strengthening of defense, not preparation for an invasion. The same approach appears in NATO’s Strategic Concept, which identifies Russia as the main direct threat to Allied security, while also specifying that the Organization does not seek confrontation with the Russian Federation. Neither NATO nor the EU has ever attacked Russia, nor have they set themselves the objective of seizing its resources. On the contrary, the EU represents one of the most enduring peace projects in the modern history of the continent, built after two world wars to prevent the reoccurrence of such conflicts.
Russia has threatened Europe with its nuclear arsenal and is already waging hybrid warfare against the West
Political scientist Andrey Suzdaltsev’s claim that no Russian official has ever threatened Europe with war is false. On February 18, 2024, former Russian President Dmitry Medvedev, the Deputy Chairman of the Security Council, threatened Berlin, London and Washington with nuclear strikes. In September 2025, the same official again warned of the risk of a nuclear war with Europe.
On the other hand, the absence of direct threats does not guarantee that Russia will refrain from using force. Just a few days before the invasion of February 24, 2022, Moscow denied Western reports about preparations for an attack. Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova mocked warnings about the imminence of war. Three days later, Russia invaded Ukraine from several directions. Kremlin statements about its peaceful intentions must therefore be assessed against its actions.
Finally, the Kremlin is contradicted by its own actions. Russia is the only power in this century that has launched wars on the European continent and attempted to alter internationally recognized borders: in Georgia in 2008 and in Ukraine in 2014 and 2022. Russia is also suspected of launching the 2007 cyberattack against Estonia, of being behind a series of assassinations of Putin opponents sheltered in Western countries, and of conducting a wave of hybrid operations (electoral interference, sabotage, drone incursions, etc.), all accompanied by an intensive disinformation campaign.
World War II broke out when Germany and the USSR attacked Poland, after concluding a pact
The article associates Germany’s rearmament with preparation for a third world war, suggesting that Berlin is returning to the expansionist policies of the Nazi era. The comparison ignores the differences between today’s democratic Germany and Hitler’s regime, as well as the responsibility of the USSR for the outbreak of the World War II.
In the case of World War II, which started on September 1, 1939 with the invasion of Poland by Nazi Germany, Moscow omits the initial collaboration between Hitler and Stalin. On August 23, 1939, the two regimes signed the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact, whose secret protocols divided Eastern Europe into spheres of influence. On September 17, the Soviet Union invaded Poland from the east. In 2019, the European Parliament condemned the collaboration between the two totalitarian regimes, emphasizing the role of the pact in paving the way to war. The comparison also ignores the distinction between militarizing a state in order to conquer foreign territories and developing defensive capabilities as a response to a war that has already been launched. Nazi Germany pursued territorial expansion by force, whereas European states are strengthening their defenses after Russia illegally annexed Ukrainian territories.
Europe is not seeking to seize Russia’s resources, nor to provoke a war
Russian political scientist Suzdaltsev, quoted by Ukraina.ru, argues that Europe is an “empire” that cannot survive economically without Russia’s resources and seeks to seize them through military conflict. However, the expert provides no evidence whatsoever that such an objective exists. Europe’s economic challenges are turned into an alleged intention of territorial conquest.
Nor does the development of the defense industry demonstrate that Europe needs to start a war in order to save its economy. Military spending may stimulate certain industrial sectors, but it also entails significant budgetary costs. Moreover, the EU is a union of states that cooperate politically and economically, not an “empire” that expands its borders through conquest. By contrast, Russia annexed Crimea in 2014 and attempted in 2022 to annex four additional Ukrainian regions, including territories it did not fully control.
The final part of the article attributes to Poland, Finland, Sweden and the Baltic States an intention to provoke a war with Russia in order to strengthen their international standing. No evidence is presented that these states seek to trigger a conflict that would bring human losses, destruction and enormous economic costs.
The example of Ukraine, invoked by Suzdaltsev, actually contradicts his own argument. Ukraine became the focus of international attention after being invaded by Russia, not because it wanted a war. The military and political support received by Kyiv is a response to aggression, not proof of a plan to provoke it. If war automatically strengthened the international position of attacked states, as the political scientist suggests, then Russia itself would, through its aggression, be contributing to the strengthening of its adversaries.
Moreover, Finland and Sweden abandoned their traditional policy of military non-alignment after the Russian invasion. Finland joined NATO in April 2023, and Sweden in March 2024. NATO enlargement was thus one of the consequences of Russia’s aggression. The article reverses the relationship between cause and effect: Russia invades Ukraine and annexes territories, yet the measures adopted by Europe to prevent the conflict from spreading are portrayed as preparations for aggression.
BACKGROUND: For many years, the Kremlin has promoted the narrative that the West is preparing a war against Russia, using it also to justify the invasion of Ukraine. Following the annexation of Crimea in 2014, the UN General Assembly reaffirmed Ukraine’s territorial integrity, and in March 2022 condemned the full-scale invasion and called for the withdrawal of Russian troops. high_priority_articles.title: France’s borrowing costs hit 5% for first time since 2002 - Financial Times
high_priority_articles.summary: France’s borrowing costs hit 5% for first time since 2002  Financial TimesFrench borrowing costs hit 24-year high as civil unrest and budget fears spook markets  The GuardianGermany’s top banker sounds alarm over French debt crisis  The TelegraphRates Spark: France still singled out  ing thinkFrench 10-year bond yields hit 5%, highest since 2002  Reuters
high_priority_articles.full_text:
Roula Khalaf, Editor of the FT, selects her favourite stories in this weekly newsletter.
France’s long-term borrowing costs have hit 5 per cent, a benchmark last reached in 2002, as investors grow increasingly concerned about the stability of the country’s politics and the state of its public finances.
A fresh bout of selling on Wednesday pushed French 10-year bond yields up as much as 0.1 percentage points to 5.02 per cent, taking the jump so far this week to more than 0.2 percentage points. The yield closed at 4.99 per cent on Wednesday afternoon.
The moves come after days of unrest and political recriminations in the country, as peaceful demonstrations over the cost of living and education spiralled into widespread rioting and looting.
France’s borrowing costs have surged from 3.2 per cent in late February, having been the hardest hit in a sweeping sell-off in G7 bond markets, as the Iran war has stoked inflation and put economies with large debt piles and wide budget deficits under particular pressure. Bond yields rise as prices fall.
“The political willingness for any fiscal consolidation ahead of the election is very, very low,” said Jeff Mueller, co-head of fixed income at Morgan Stanley Investment Management, adding there was plenty of room for “the situation to worsen from here”.
The closely watched gap, or spread, between French 10-year borrowing costs and Germany’s rose to almost 1.6 percentage points on Wednesday, matching the intraday high reached in volatile trading earlier this month.
Such a level had previously not been seen since the Eurozone debt crisis more than a decade ago.
Other Eurozone bond markets also suffered on Wednesday, with Italy’s 10-year yield rising 0.07 percentage points to 4.59 per cent, although it is below the post-2023 high it hit earlier this month.
Belgium’s 10-year yield jumped as much as 0.12 percentage points to 4.46 per cent, taking its spread with Germany back to just above one percentage point, its highest intraday level since 2013. It later fell back to 4.43 per cent.
The country, which has one of the biggest budget deficits in the euro area and a higher-than-average debt load at 108 per cent of GDP, is at present holding difficult budget talks.
Prime Minister Bart De Wever has vowed to reduce spending, but discussions stalled again this week as leftwing and liberal coalition partners sparred over proposed cuts.
De Wever told parliament on Wednesday that if the financial situation was not stabilised, “I fear the outbreak of a debt crisis, for which we need to prepare”.
Investors view a broader serious downturn in Eurozone government bond markets beyond France as a key precondition for any intervention by the European Central Bank to support the market.
Lorenzo Bini Smaghi, a former ECB board member, wrote in the FT earlier this month that widening spreads showed “the shadows of the 2011-12 crisis are emerging again”. He said the euro area was in a stronger position, but the ECB could support the market by putting on hold its balance-sheet-shrinking programme, known as quantitative tightening.
Moody’s will issue a ratings decision on France on Friday, with a downgrade a real possibility given the outlook is already negative on the current rating of Aa3.
“The political situation is pretty adverse and [it is] difficult to see that improving anytime soon,” said John Stopford, head of multi-asset income at asset manager Ninety One.
The “path of least resistance”, Stopford added, was for a wider French spread heading towards April’s presidential election, arguing that the ECB would be unlikely to step in without a significant deterioration from current levels.

high_priority_articles.summary: In China, ECB makes case for euro liquidity lines  AOL.co.uk
high_priority_articles.full_text:
FRANKFURT, Oct 21 (Reuters) - The European Central Bank can strengthen the euro's global role and amplify the reach of its monetary policy by providing liquidity safety nets to foreign countries, ECB chief economist Philip Lane said on Wednesday.
Speaking at a closed-door event in Shanghai titled "Monetary System Beyond the Dollar", Lane said demand for the ECB's recently expanded euro liquidity facilities had been strong, with more than 30 central banks expressing interest.
"Liquidity lines bolster confidence in the currency and reduce the associated risks, supporting its wider usage," he told the event, part of the annual Bund summit, according to prepared remarks.
The comments come as policymakers globally question the the long-term dominance of the dollar in light of US President Donald Trump's unpredictable economic policy.
Lane argued that greater international use of the euro would enhance the ECB's ability to deliver on its inflation mandate by extending the global impact of euro area monetary policy.
He said the ECB's EUREP facility, which allows foreign central banks to obtain euros against collateral denominated in the single currency, could boost bond markets in the 21-country bloc, particularly through increased purchases by official reserve managers.
ECB President Christine Lagarde said recently that the bank was also reviewing its network of currency swap lines, which allow major central banks, including the US Federal Reserve and the People's Bank of China, to exchange their own currencies for euros.
Lane said such arrangements can encourage borrowing in euros but should be reserved for central banks in economies with close financial links to the euro area and a clear capacity to repay euro liabilities.

high_priority_articles.title: South Korea Dominates HBM for AI Chips - 조선일보
high_priority_articles.summary: South Korea Dominates HBM for AI Chips  조선일보
high_priority_articles.full_text:
In the race to lead in artificial intelligence (AI), the demand for superior AI processing chips and more memory semiconductors has intensified the global semiconductor industry’s endless competition over manufacturing technologies.
The most intense battleground lies in memory semiconductors, particularly HBM (high-bandwidth memory) used in AI accelerators like those from NVIDIA. The most advanced product is the 6th-generation HBM4, which only three companies—Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix, and U.S.-based Micron—can produce.
Chinese memory firms still struggle to produce HBM effectively. According to Counterpoint Research, SK Hynix held a 50% market share in HBM in the second quarter of this year, followed by Samsung Electronics at 33%. Micron ranked third with 18%. The industry estimates that Chinese HBM technology lags South Korea by over three years.
In contrast, Chinese firms are gaining ground in the general DRAM and NAND flash markets. In the second-quarter global DRAM market, Chinese ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) claimed a 10% share, ranking fourth behind Samsung Electronics (38%), SK Hynix (25%), and Micron (24%).
While South Korean products still lead technologically, the AI boom-driven DRAM shortage has opened opportunities for CXMT. South Korean semiconductor companies’ most advanced DRAM is the 1c process (early 10-nanometer class, with 1 nanometer equaling one-billionth of a meter). Comparing Samsung’s 1983-developed 64Kb DRAM to today’s 1c-process 24Gb DRAM used in HBM4, chip capacity has grown approximately 390,000 times, while circuit line widths have shrunk to a fraction of their original size. Meanwhile, CXMT’s recently mass-produced process technology is five years behind Samsung’s. However, CXMT has announced plans to adopt the 4F² design technology—reducing DRAM cell area—within the year, effectively declaring its intent to overtake Samsung and SK Hynix.
In NAND flash, Chinese Yangtze Memory Technologies Corporation (YMTC) is rapidly closing the gap. In the second-quarter shipment rankings, YMTC held a 16.5% share, placing third behind Samsung and SK Hynix. Its technological prowess is notable: leveraging its proprietary “Xtacking” stacking technology, YMTC is developing products exceeding 300 layers. The industry consensus is that South Korea and China now have virtually no technological gap in NAND flash.
The non-memory (system semiconductor) sector is dominated by the U.S. and Taiwan. The CPU market is split between U.S. firms Intel and AMD, while NVIDIA commands over 80% of the GPU market. Though Chinese companies like Huawei have developed their own GPUs and AI chips, their performance lags behind U.S. counterparts.
In foundry (semiconductor contract manufacturing), Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) leads with a 72.5% global market share in the second quarter, according to TrendForce. Samsung Electronics ranked second with 5.9%, followed by China’s Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (SMIC) at 5.4%. Both TSMC and Samsung have entered the 2-nanometer process, but TSMC is reported to have a significant lead in yield rates.

high_priority_articles.full_text:
The AI (artificial intelligence)-driven semiconductor super cycle has completely reshaped the global trade landscape in just one year. According to an analysis by Chosun Ilbo and KOTRA, Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency, of World Trade Organization (WTO) and major countries’ statistics on the 21st, the owners of six positions from 5th to 10th among the world’s top 10 exporters in the first half of this year have changed. This is the most turbulent shift since 2009, when China overtook Germany to claim the top spot during the global financial crisis.
At the eye of the typhoon is South Korea, the world’s leading memory powerhouse. South Korea is on the verge of achieving its first-ever exports of 1 trillion dollars (semiconductors are projected to reach 400 billion dollars) this year. With its first-half exports (496.1 billion dollars) surging 48.2% compared to the same period last year, it jumped from 7th place last year to 5th. Not only did it overtake Japan, long considered an insurmountable rival, but it also closed in on the Netherlands (531.5 billion dollars), a global intermediary trade powerhouse and a member of the top four.
Korean memory chips have propelled trading partners’ rankings through global supply chains. Taiwan, which imports Korean HBM (high-bandwidth memory) to assemble AI accelerators, rose from 11th to 6th. Mexico, which assembles servers for the U.S. using Asian semiconductor components, climbed from 10th to 8th. Singapore, a semiconductor back-end and intermediary hub, entered the top 10 from 13th. Meanwhile, traditional manufacturing powerhouse Japan fell from 5th to 9th, while 3rd-place Germany stagnated. Semiconductors are reshaping global trade power.
◇Powered by the Semiconductor Engine… South Korea’s Exports Surge 48%, Taiwan’s 46% in First Half
South Korea’s semiconductor exports surpassed 60 billion dollars in a single month for the first time last month. This is nearly equivalent to Japan’s average monthly total exports (64.7 billion dollars) this year. A single product—semiconductors—now matches Japan’s entire export volume. Currently, an average of 4.74 billion dollars worth of “Made in Korea” goods are shipped worldwide every day, exceeding 50,000 dollars per second.
Explosive semiconductor exports are altering the global trade map. Until last year, Japan was the world’s 5th-largest exporter, behind only China, the U.S., Germany, and the Netherlands, with Italy ahead of 7th-place South Korea. However, within a year, the “semiconductor gold rush” triggered by global Big Tech’s AI (artificial intelligence) data center expansion has propelled South Korea and other AI supply chain nations upward, while traditional manufacturing powers reliant on automobiles and chemicals have fallen behind.
① Beyond Overtaking Japan for the First Time, South Korea Eyes the Netherlands’ Top Four Status
In 2005, South Korea’s exports (284.4 billion dollars) were less than half (48%) of Japan’s (595.3 billion dollars). Twenty-one years later, in 2026, South Korea has finally distanced itself from Japan by a wide margin. From January to August this year, South Korea’s exports reached 693.6 billion dollars, surpassing Japan’s 517.4 billion dollars by 176.2 billion dollars. South Korea’s export growth rate (52.9%) during this period was nearly three times that of China (18.3%) and seven times Japan’s (7.7%). Semiconductors accounted for 74% of the increase.
South Korea’s semiconductor exports from January to August surged 171.7% year-on-year to 280 billion dollars, a net increase of 176.9 billion dollars from last year. In contrast, Japan’s automotive exports—a key sector—grew by only 2.2% (78.1 billion dollars), a mere 1.7 billion dollar increase. South Korea’s semiconductor export growth rate was over 100 times that of Japan’s automotive sector.
South Korea is now threatening 4th-place Netherlands. The gap with the Netherlands, based on first-half figures, is only 35.4 billion dollars. South Korea is poised to surpass the European intermediary trade hub, which fills half of its exports through re-exports, purely through manufacturing strength. At the current pace, entering the “world’s top four” is no longer a distant dream, analysts say.
② The Butterfly Effect of K-Memory… Taiwan, Mexico, and Singapore Leap Forward
Korean memory chips have lifted trading partners’ export rankings through global division of labor. Taiwan, a foundry powerhouse that exclusively outsources GPU production, saw its exports jump 46.1% in the first half, rising five spots from 11th to 6th. AI accelerators assembled by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) and exported to U.S. Big Tech include Korean HBM. This explains why South Korea’s exports to Taiwan surged 61.3% to 47.5 billion dollars from January to August.
The ripple effect extended to Mexico and Southeast Asia. Mexico, which rose to 8th place in global exports, has transformed into an AI server assembly base targeting the North American market. From January to August, South Korea’s semiconductor exports to Mexico exploded by 293.4%, and computer component exports surged 725.0%. Singapore, which entered the top 10 for the first time, also capitalized on the AI boom as a Southeast Asian logistics hub that packages and re-exports semiconductors from neighboring countries.
③ Relative Decline of Traditional Manufacturing Powers Japan and Germany
Manufacturing powers outside the AI supply chain or reliant on traditional industries struggled. Japan, which fell to 9th place with a 6.5% export growth rate in the first half, is a prime example. While some sectors like semiconductor manufacturing equipment performed well, its largest export—automobiles—was hampered by U.S. tariff barriers and sluggish demand in China. Structural factors, such as Japan’s overseas production share rising from 11.8% in 2000 to 25.3% in 2024, further reduced domestic export statistics. Germany, the world’s 3rd-largest exporter, also lagged behind South Korea and Taiwan with a mere 10.8% export growth rate in the first half. Affected by low-cost competition from Chinese electric vehicles, Germany’s automotive exports fell 10.6% from January to June.
Park Min-jun, head of KOTRA’s Trade and Investment Research Center, said, “To solidify South Korea’s position as a top-five exporter and achieve the 1 trillion dollar milestone, the country must diversify its export engines into bio, defense, and consumer goods, leveraging its ultra-competitive semiconductor sector as a fulcrum.”

high_priority_articles.summary: U.S.-South Korea-Taiwan Semiconductor Dominance Faces Chinese Challenge  조선일보
high_priority_articles.full_text:
Apple, a U.S. tech giant, is a major player in the global semiconductor market. Its iPhones and MacBooks are equipped with memory chips like DRAM and NAND flash, as well as in-house developed application processors (APs). Last year, Apple procured over 19 billion chips from U.S. supply chains, mostly from South Korean, U.S., and Taiwanese companies.
Recently, Apple has been considering the use of DRAM from Chinese ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT). John Ternus, Apple’s chief operating officer, stated on the 15th, “We must review all options, including Chinese-made memory.” While actual adoption remains uncertain due to U.S. regulations and political opposition, Apple’s shift reflects the changing realities of the semiconductor industry.
The global semiconductor industry has long been led by the U.S. in technology and standards, with South Korea and Taiwan supporting manufacturing in memory and foundry sectors, respectively. However, China is now disrupting this structure by leveraging massive capital, strong government policies, and a vast domestic market to rapidly advance its production and technological capabilities.
Some analysts predict that by 2030, China will become the world’s largest semiconductor producer. Concerns are growing that the global semiconductor dominance long held by South Korea, the U.S., and Taiwan could shift to China, starting with memory chips. Chris Miller, a professor at Tufts University, wrote in his book *Chip War*, “Semiconductors have shaped the structure of international politics, the global economy, and the balance of military power.”
◇Industry Built by the U.S., Division of Labor with Korea and Taiwan
Semiconductors are essential components for products requiring information processing, from computers and smartphones to home appliances, automobiles, and toys. A single smartphone contains dozens of chips, while a car can have up to 3,000, from engine control units to headlights. Artificial intelligence (AI), a cornerstone of the Fourth Industrial Revolution, also relies on semiconductors.
The modern semiconductor industry began in the U.S. with the invention of the transistor in 1947. Fairchild Semiconductor, founded in 1957, laid the foundation for mass production of integrated circuits (ICs), and Intel, established in 1968, ushered in the era of CPUs and DRAM in the 1970s. Companies like Intel and Texas Instruments led the integrated semiconductor industry, handling design, production, and packaging.
In the 1980s, Japan challenged U.S. dominance by leveraging its manufacturing base and large-scale investments to dominate the memory market. By 1986, Japan became the world’s largest semiconductor supplier, with an 80% share of the DRAM market the following year. Facing this pressure, the U.S. signed the U.S.-Japan Semiconductor Agreement in September 1986, which included measures to curb Japan’s dominance. A surging yen eroded Japan’s price competitiveness, and missed investment opportunities led to its decline.
South Korea and Taiwan filled the gap. Samsung Electronics developed 64K DRAM in 1983 and became the world’s top DRAM producer in 1992 by releasing the first 64M DRAM, overtaking Japan. Taiwan took a different path: Morris Chang, a former TI executive, founded TSMC in 1987 with government support, establishing the foundry model.
The semiconductor industry then split into fabless design, foundry, and integrated device manufacturing, forming a global division of labor. U.S. fabless companies like NVIDIA, AMD, and Qualcomm focused on design, accelerating advancements in GPUs for AI and other semiconductors.
◇China Challenges Semiconductor Hegemony with Capital and Domestic Market
China, once a peripheral player, is now challenging the U.S.-South Korea-Taiwan semiconductor alliance. Starting with the founding of foundry SMIC in 2000, China entered the memory market in 2016 by establishing CXMT and Yangtze Memory Technologies (YMTC), recruiting talent from Korean firms.
Its production expansion, fueled by government subsidies and domestic demand, is remarkable. CXMT’s monthly DRAM wafer production capacity is estimated to grow from 20,000 wafers in 2019 to about 350,000 by the end of this year—a 17.5-fold increase. This nears Samsung’s capacity (about 720,000 wafers) and approaches U.S. Micron’s (about 385,000 wafers).
Technological progress is also alarming. Huawei released the Ascend AI accelerator to rival NVIDIA, and CXMT announced plans to launch next-generation server DRAM before Samsung and SK Hynix. Counterpoint Research noted, “U.S. export restrictions have paradoxically accelerated China’s semiconductor development, giving it a chance to catch up.”
The European Court of Auditors (ECA) projected that China’s share of global semiconductor production capacity will rise from 11% in 2010 to 22% by 2030, becoming the largest producer. A high-ranking official from the domestic industry said, “China’s semiconductor growth is already a major threat to the Korean economy. We must widen the gap in HBM, next-generation DRAM, and NAND.”

At the start of October, Nvidia announced that it would soon be adding Microsoft's Advanced Shader Delivery (ASD) technology to its RTX and RTX Spark graphics drivers in the continuing fight against the shader compilation stutter that has become increasingly commonplace in modern PC gaming. With version 621.01, released today, ASD support is now finally in place.
ASD is designed to prevent the momentary hitches experienced in games when a shader needs to be compiled on the fly, often when a new model or effect appears for the first time. Most modern games include a shader burn when you first launch a game (or update your graphics drivers), but it's still common for some shaders to be missed by this step. ASD works by downloading precompiled shaders from the cloud for your specific graphics hardware on Windows 11. It's a similar approach to the Linux-based Steam Shader Pre-Caching system established by Valve for the Steam Deck.
This normally "just works", with no user involvement, though developers need to specifically support the technology. If you want to test it out, two high-profile releases with support are Gears of War: E-Day and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.
As well as eliminating troublesome shader compilation stutter, the technology also massively speeds up that initial precompilation step - Microsoft says it is reduced by up to 95 percent. Given that this can take upwards of 20 minutes even on high-end systems in some games, that's a meaningful improvement.
However, this technology doesn't help prevent traversal stutter, another hitch-causing phenomenon related to data being loaded into and out of memory when passing an invisible boundary in the game world.
Nvidia also has a technology to prevent shaders from being wiped out following a graphics driver update called Automatic Shader Compilation, and the two technologies can be used in concert.
To benefit from Advanced Shader Delivery support, you'll need to be using Windows 11 24H2 or later and update to Nvidia's 621.01 driver via the Nvidia app or by manually downloading the installer - I had to opt for the latter as the driver wasn't showing as available in the app for my PC.
Note that ASD is already part of AMD and Qualcomm's graphics driver and is also set to arrive for Intel discrete and integrated graphics later this month, though an official release date or graphics driver version number has not yet been set.

high_priority_articles.full_text:
Isometric Approves Five Insurers for Reforestation Carbon Credit Protection
- Insurance framework: Isometric will allow eligible reforestation projects to replace part of their carbon-credit buffer contributions with insurance.
- Five approved providers: Artio, CarbonPool, CFC, Kita and Oka can offer coverage to projects certified by Isometric.
- Project revenue: Developers could retain more carbon removal certificates for sale while maintaining protection against carbon reversals.
Carbon removal registry Isometric has launched an insurance framework with broker Marsh to improve the financial flexibility of certified reforestation projects. The framework allows developers to replace part of their buffer pool contributions with approved insurance policies. Five insurance providers have received approval to participate.
Buffer pools reserve carbon removal certificates against reversals, which occur when stored carbon returns to the atmosphere. Wildfires and disease are among the risks covered by these safeguards. Under Isometric’s new arrangement, eligible developers could retain more certificates for sale, particularly during a project’s early years.
Artio, CarbonPool, CFC, Kita and Oka are the five approved insurance providers. Each can offer coverage to reforestation projects certified by Isometric. Other insurers may apply to join the framework as the registry expands participation.
Isometric said its requirements integrate insurance with existing buffer mechanisms rather than removing reversal protection. The framework aims to ensure each certificate retired by a buyer still represents one tonne of carbon dioxide (CO2) removed. However, Isometric did not disclose insurance pricing, coverage limits, eligibility thresholds or an implementation date.
Bruno Figueiredo, Vice President of Finance at reforestation developer Mombak, described the framework as “an important step toward a more mature carbon market.” He said insurance could improve certainty for buyers and strengthen how projects manage reversal risks.
RELATED ARTICLE: Isometric Expands Carbon Removal Certification to China
Meanwhile, Hema Mistry, Chief Executive of FINPRO UK at Marsh Risk, said “integrating insurance into market infrastructure could help developers expand projects. She also identified greater confidence among buyers, lenders and investors as a potential benefit.”
Isometric is considering extending the framework beyond reforestation to other carbon removal pathways. Developers interested in participating can contact the registry for further information about its requirements. The registry has not identified which additional removal pathways it may include.
Why It Matters
Isometric gains an insurance-backed option within its certification framework, while Marsh extends its role in carbon removal risk management. For developers certified by Isometric, the arrangement could increase the share of certificates available for sale. If insurance costs justify reduced buffer contributions, developers could generate more early-stage certificate revenue to support project expansion.

high_priority_articles.title: Iran's Ghalibaf meets Khamenei amid US-Israel tensions
high_priority_articles.summary: Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf held talks with Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei on the latest military and economic developments involving the United...
high_priority_articles.full_text:
Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf held talks with Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei on the latest military and economic developments involving the United States and Israel, as well as information warfare, Fars News Agency reported Wednesday.
The meeting focused on strengthening Iran’s national capabilities, maintaining social cohesion and national unity, and improving cooperation between the government and parliament to address economic and livelihood challenges.
The two also emphasized advancing relations with Iran’s strategic partners, the same source said.
Ghalibaf briefed Khamenei on parliamentary activities since the outbreak of the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran on Feb. 28 and outlined ongoing and future plans to address the country’s challenges.
The meeting marks another rare reported encounter involving Khamenei, who has not made a public appearance since succeeding his father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, in March.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian earlier said he had met Khamenei twice since he assumed office in March, including a meeting in August that lasted more than seven hours.
Khamenei was selected as Iran’s supreme leader on March 8, following the death of his father in U.S.-Israeli strikes on Feb. 28.
Since assuming leadership, Khamenei has communicated primarily through written statements, while his absence from public view has fueled speculation about his condition and role in the country’s decision-making.
The latest meeting comes amid continuing tensions between Tehran and Washington over security arrangements in the Strait of Hormuz and their broader conflict.
